A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NeCGS for compressing 3D geometry sets. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression comparisons on AMA, DT4D, Thingi10K, and Mixed, together with ablations and reconstructed-shape results.

after.justification: v2 retains original compression experiments and reports additional regularization, timing, resolution, and incremental shape-compression results.

M1.justification: v2 adds L1 deformation regularization to Equation (1) and an incremental procedure that optimizes new shapes' embedded features while freezing the trained decoder. These are limited extensions of the retained TSDF-Def, quantization-aware auto-decoder, Huffman coding, and DMC pipeline.

E1.justification: The four datasets and principal dataset sizes are retained. v2 adds a distinct incremental scenario in which new Thingi10K shapes enter an already compressed set (Figure 12), extending the previous fixed-set evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 2 makes the unregularized predecessor an explicit comparator, labeled TSDF-Def w/o L1 Reg., against the regularized proposal alongside TSDF. The external baselines remain GPCC, VPCC, PCGCv2, Draco, and QuantDeepSDF; QuantDeepSDF's construction is unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes from decompressed-model evaluation described as AMA in v1 to representation accuracy on 100 thin/fine Mixed shapes in v2; these are not matched experimental settings. v2 also introduces set-level compression and per-model decompression timing, frozen-decoder insertion evaluation, and a K=32 configuration. The main training budgets, metrics, and surface-point sampling remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a regularization control, a focused fine-structure representation study, runtime comparisons, and frozen-decoder generalization examples. Resolution sensitivity extends to K=32, and additional complex-shape cases examine detail preservation. The existing auto-encoder and SSIM analyses remain, with revised curves.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The random surface-point sampling used to compute reconstruction metrics is unchanged.

E6.justification: NeCGS's main and ablation rate-distortion curves change, and Table 2 reports replacement results under different conditions. Within v2's regularization comparison, CD changes from 6.205 to 5.396 (×10^-3) between unregularized and regularized TSDF-Def. Added results include timing, K=32 performance, and new reconstruction examples. Table 3 retains the K=64/128/256 accuracy values but removes their optimization times.

T1.justification: Equation (1) changes the formal optimization problem from reconstruction-only minimization to reconstruction plus a weighted L1 deformation penalty. The TSDF-Def definition, quantization formula, and evaluation equations otherwise remain equivalent; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly claim successful continual addition of shapes to an existing compressed set. The introduction also explicitly lists a benchmark contribution. The principal claims about compressing diverse geometry sets with high reconstruction fidelity remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for suppressing unnecessary deformation and interprets insertion examples as decoder generalization. It removes v1's point-cloud applicability note and explicit limitations concerning over-15-hour optimization and slow 3D-convolution inference. The new practical discussion instead emphasizes offline compression and prioritizes decompression speed.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project source-code access statement, specifies OBJ storage and lambda_Reg=10, and documents removing two decoder layers for K=32. Most implementation and supplementary settings remain unchanged. The resolution study is explicitly identified as AMA, while its optimization-time breakdown is removed.

R1.justification: The cited works remain the same; the supplement's DeepSDF and PixelShuffle references repeat existing citations. Positioning is refined through an expanded contrast between conventional SDF/TSDF resolution requirements and uniform compact TSDF-Def tensors, plus the explicit benchmark contribution.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the TSDF-Def exposition is reorganized into definition, remark, and optimization passages. Terminology changes from volumes to tensors throughout. The conclusion loses its discussion paragraph, and the appendices become separately titled and numbered supplementary material.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from one to two columns. Figure 3 is expanded, plot legends and axes are redesigned, tables are restructured, and new timing, complex-shape, and dynamic-scenario displays appear. v1's appendix Figure 13 is enlarged and separated into v2 Figures 17–19 rather than constituting new results.

improvement.justification: The regularization control in Table 2, added efficiency comparisons, clearer method exposition, and code-access disclosure provide a modest gain in evidential support and reproducibility. This is tempered by removal of explicit limitations and optimization-time breakdowns, unspecified dataset/rate settings for the timing comparison, and only qualitative support for the new dynamic-scenario claim.
